title: A Bright, Limitless Future
subtitle: But something else lies beyond that distant horizon.

items.speaker: Turbine
items.text: We have arrived at your destination, the Polymer Exhibition Hall. Please be careful when exiting the vehicle.
Entrance, Polymer Exhibition Hall
The Turbine lands, and the Bumblebee retracts its cables. Now settled on the ground, the young visitors undo their seatbelts and exit the car.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Wow, it's so crowded! Why is everyone gathered around the entrance?
A few robots in receptionist uniforms are bustling around, trying to keep the hordes of scientists in front of the exhibition hall in line.
Everyone, please wait patiently and enter the venue in an orderly fashion. Dr. Sechenov is about to arrive!

items.speaker: Scientist III
items.text: He's here! He's here!
Amid the hubbub, a black Turbine lands outside the crowd. Several robots hurry forward to open the door.
Welcome, comrade.

items.speaker: Scientist IV
items.text: It's him! That's Dr. Sechenov!
The crowd erupts as people rush forward, eager to shake hands with the savior of the Soviet Union.
The sudden surge from behind makes it difficult to stay standing.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hm?
Please be careful.
A pair of powerful metal arms catches the body and keeps it balanced.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you.
It is good that you were unharmed, comrade.
Having resolved this minor incident, the two robots return to Dr. Sechenov's side, helping him navigate the crowd.

items.speaker: Sechenov
items.text: Please don't push, everyone! We must all be patient! I ask that you be mindful of the safety of your comrades in the front row!
As Sechenov enters the venue, the scientists follow in after him, draining the entryway like water through a funnel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That must be Sechenov, and I suppose those women were the Twins?

items.speaker: X
items.text: A logical hypothesis. Oh, Vertin, we do have a slight problem.

items.speaker: X
items.text: The communicator must've slipped out of my pocket during the commotion. By the time I found it again, well, it seems to have failed a few rapid percussive tests.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Which means we've lost our only way to contact Madam Lucy.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Unfortunate, but we'll fix it later. We should follow the crowd into the exhibition hall for now.
As the visitors cross through the front doors, the entire gallery opens up before them.
Streamlined, recessed strip lights highlight the various exhibits on display. In the distance, there's some kind of interactive installation illustrating the unique properties of polymer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "The Invention of Polymer and Its Uses" ... "The Properties of Polymer" ... "The Establishment of Kollektiv" ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hmm. Where should we start?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Let's start with the closest one.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: Hello, dear comrades! Welcome to the Polymer Exhibition Hall! I will be your guide. You may call me Tereshkova!

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: Please allow me to introduce you to the remarkable history of polymer.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: In 1936, in seeking a form of liquid data carrier, the brilliant Soviet scientist, Dr. Sechenov, influenced by the qualities of heavy water and silicon, created a substance that became what we now know as "polymer."

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: Utilizing polymer's unique electrochemical properties, Comrades Sechenov and Filimonenko invented the first Soviet polymer hydrogen cell in 1939, paving the way for tremendous advancements in the field of robotics!

items.speaker: X
items.text: That's what Maxim was telling us about, wasn't it? I'm sure Madam Lucy would love to get her hands on one.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: However, in 1942, a terrible disaster struck the Soviet Union and the entire European continent—the Plague! By the end of this unprecedented outbreak, over 150 million had perished.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: 150 million? That would make it one of the deadliest outbreaks in human history.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: Countless scientists and medical professionals selflessly gave their lives to combatting this Plague, sacrificing themselves to prevent further death ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I wonder if that's the tragedy that Maxim mentioned.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: We will always remember their sacrifice! Just as we honor Dr. Sechenov for once again coming to our rescue!

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: It was his polymer that formed the basis of Redemption, the vaccine that proved instrumental in stopping the transmission of the disease, saving the Soviet Union from ravages of the Plague!

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: Of course, with so many having succumbed to the disease, the Soviet Union turned to further developments in robotics to meet labor demands.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: Before long, new advanced models of robots made up a significant portion of our labor force, helping to deliver a new age of prosperity.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Is that what you've been aiming at with all of your Critter experiments, X?

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: In order to fully optimize our robots' production power, Dr. Sechenov led a team of scientists to develop and launch Kollektiv 1.0!

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: This revolutionary system unified all of our robot assistants under a single vast neural network, ensuring maximum efficiency!

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: Then in 1950, Dr. Sechenov astounded the world with yet another development: A means of incorporating polymer into the human body, a process called Polymer Assimilative Adaptation.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: It is with this assimilative power that we can now implant interface devices directly into the human body, allowing people to connect to Kollektiv 1.0 and control robots using their minds.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: This technology holds the potential to establish a shared database of human minds, granting humanity unprecedented access to knowledge.

items.speaker: Tereshkova
items.text: And we are proud to announce that this potential will soon be realized with the coming launch of Kollektiv 2.0!

items.speaker: X
items.text: Tapping into an entire neural network in an instant? It's a daring vision.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I would be cautious. There's no telling what that kind of process could do to the human brain.
